question: How do I evaluate whether a new vertical is worth the GTM investment?
answer:
**Direct Answer:** Model 18-month unit economics before investing. Target vertical must have >$100M TAM addressable by you, <3% CAC increase vs core vertical, and repeatable buyer profile. If CAC payback exceeds 15 months or projected NRR <105%, wait for product fit improvements before expanding. **The Detail** Most founders expand verticals blind. Build an evaluation scorecard. **Vertical evaluation scorecard (weight each 1–5 points):** | Factor | Scoring | Notes | |--------|---------|-------| | **TAM** | $100M+ reachable = 5pts | Estimate addressable universe in vertical | | **Buyer profile match** | Exact match to core = 5pts | Same titles, same buying process? | | **Product fit (no customization)** | Core product works unmodified = 5pts | Do you need vertical-specific features? | | **CAC predictability** | Similar CAC to core = 5pts | Can you reuse marketing, messaging? | | **Competitive intensity** | <5 competitors = 5pts | Fewer entrenched players = easier entry | | **GDD (go-to-decision time)** | 3–6 months = 5pts | How long is sales cycle? | | **Expansion potential** | NRR target ≥105% = 5pts | Will customers expand within vertical? | | **Customer reference availability** | 3+ customers in vertical = 5pts | Can you build case studies? | **Scoring system:** - 35–40 points: Excellent expansion candidate. Launch within 6 months. - 28–34 points: Good fit. De-risk with pilot (3–5 logos). - 20–27 points: Risky. Requires product investment first. - <20 points: Don't pursue. Opportunity cost too high. **Build 18-month unit economics model:** **Inputs (estimate or research):** 1. **Addressable market** - List universe of companies in vertical (Crunchbase, industry database) - Filter by your fit (employee count, revenue, use-case match) - Addressable universe = 15–20% of full vertical - Example: Healthcare staffing has 8,000 agencies; you can reach 1,200. 2. **CAC and close rate** - Research: How will you acquire leads? (LinkedIn, trade shows, partner channels) - Estimate cost to acquire 1 qualified lead: $200–500 depending on vertical - Estimated close rate: 15–30% (benchmark to your core vertical) - CAC = (spend per month × 18 months) ÷ (logos closed) 3. **ACV and ramp** - Will ACV be higher/lower than core? (healthcare regulatory usually = higher) - Estimate Year 1 ACV: $40k (SMB) to $150k (mid-market) - Year 2+: ACV growth 10–15% from expansion 4. **Implementation complexity** - Core vertical: 4 weeks, 1 CSM involved - New vertical: 6–8 weeks (compliance, integrations added)? Adds cost. - Implementation cost: $5k–15k per customer 5. **CAC payback and profitability** - CAC payback = (CAC) ÷ (Monthly ACV × Gross Margin %) - Example: $25k CAC ÷ ($5k monthly ACV × 85% margin) = 5.9 months ✓ Good - Example: $25k CAC ÷ ($2k monthly ACV × 80% margin) = 15.6 months ✗ High risk **18-month projection template:** ``` Vertical: Healthcare Staffing Months 1–6 (Pilot / Proof-of-concept) - Deploy 1 AE + 1 SDR (shared resources) - Target: 3–5 logos - Est. cost: $150k (salaries, marketing test) - Est. revenue: $120k (3 × $40k ACV, ramp) Months 7–12 (Scale if metrics hit) - Add 2 more AEs (total 3) - Target: 8–12 cumulative logos - Est. cost: $400k (AE salaries, full marketing budget) - Est. revenue: $420k (run-rate from 12 logos @ $35k) Months 13–18 (Profitability test) - 3 AEs producing - Target: 15–20 cumulative logos - Est. revenue: $700k ARR (20 × $35k) - Est. cost: $500k (fully burdened AE + SDR team) - Operating margin: $200k ÷ $700k = 29% ✓ ``` **Go-no-go decision rules (after 6 months):** - **Go:** If you have 3–5 logos, CAC payback <10 months, NRR signal ≥105% - **Go:** If CAC is 20% lower than core vertical (pricing power) - **No-go:** If CAC payback >12 months and close rate <15% - **No-go:** If no clear customer reference for case study - **No-go:** If you need >4 engineering sprints to customize product **Vertical expansion vs marginal return:** - If core vertical is already $50M ARR, and new vertical projects $5M by year 3, the opportunity cost may be too high (opportunity: grow core to $75M instead) - But if core is capped at $100M TAM, new vertical is **required** ```mermaid flowchart TB A["New Vertical Opportunity"] --> B["Score Evaluation Card

6-month gate"] F --> H H --> I{"Metrics Hit?"} I -->|"Yes"| J["Expand to 3+ AEs"] I -->|"No"| K["Kill or Pivot"] ``` TAGS: vertical-expansion,market-entry,unit-economics,go-to-market,risk-assessment
